issues.legal_issue: A government promise of a tax exemption may be enforced by promissory estoppel despite the absence of an implementing notification when the promise was relied upon, statutory authority to grant the exemption existed, and no overriding public interest justified departure from the promise.
material_facts: The government announced that qualifying tourism-related buildings, including classified hotels, would receive a building-tax exemption and later enacted a provision authorizing exemptions to promote tourism.
The hotel developer relied on the announcement and constructed a hotel that was completed while the exemption-authorizing provision remained in force.
No exemption notification was issued for the hotel, and the government did not establish an overriding public interest that justified refusing the promised exemption.
issues.conclusion: The absence of an exemption notification did not defeat the claim. Building tax was not payable for the period during which the statutory power to grant the promised exemption was in force.
issues.legal_principle: Under M/S Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills v. State of Uttar Pradesh, a government promise intended to induce action is enforceable when the promisee relies on it and alters its position; detriment need not be separately proved. The government bears the burden of establishing, on adequate material, that overriding public interest makes enforcement inequitable. State of Punjab v. Nestle India Ltd. confirms that the failure to issue the necessary notification does not itself defeat relief where the government had power to grant the exemption and was bound by its promise. Pournami Oil Mills and Devi Multiplex apply the same principle. Equity may treat as done what ought to have been done.

rule.if: is_appeal_from_tax_exemption_denial and government_made_clear_exemption_promise and promisee_relied_and_changed_position and statutory_exemption_power_existed_during_claimed_period and exemption_notification_was_not_issued and not government_established_overriding_public_interest

predicates.is_appeal_from_tax_exemption_denial: The matter is an appeal arising from the denial of a claimed tax exemption.
predicates.government_made_clear_exemption_promise: The government made a clear representation that qualifying activity or property would receive a tax exemption.
predicates.promisee_relied_and_changed_position: The person to whom the representation was made relied on it and changed position by acting on that basis.
predicates.statutory_exemption_power_existed_during: A law authorized the government to grant the claimed kind of exemption during the period for which relief is sought.
predicates.exemption_notification_was_not_issued: The government did not issue the notification contemplated for implementing the exemption.
predicates.government_established_overriding_public: The government established, on adequate material, that overriding public interest required it not to honour the promise.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a denied tax exemption, the government made a clear exemption promise, the promisee relied on it and changed position, statutory authority existed during the claimed period, no implementing notification was issued, and the government did not establish overriding public interest, the exemption is allowed for the period that authority existed.

issues.legal_issue: A court may remedy arbitrary non-exercise of a statutory discretionary power to give effect to a government promise without directing the executive to enact general rules or the legislature to amend a law.
material_facts: The government had made a specific promise of exemption and the promisee had relied on it by constructing a qualifying hotel.

The legislature enacted a provision conferring discretionary authority to grant the promised exemption, but the government did not issue the notification needed to apply it to the hotel and refused the claim.
The requested relief concerned the exercise of an existing discretionary power, not the creation of general rules or an order requiring the legislature to enact a law.
issues.conclusion: The government’s non-exercise of the discretionary power was arbitrary because it failed to take account of the promise and the reliance on it. The missing notification, which was a ministerial act in the circumstances, did not prevent relief.
issues.legal_principle: State of Jammu & Kashmir v. A.R. Zakki and State of Uttar Pradesh v. Mahindra and Mahindra Ltd. establish that a court cannot issue mandamus requiring the executive to frame subordinate legislation. But discretionary statutory powers are reviewable under administrative-law standards, including the Wednesbury principle, for matters such as failure to consider relevant facts or consideration of irrelevant ones. Indian Express Newspapers v. Union of India recognizes such review even where the power is exercised through subordinate legislation. M/S Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills and State of Punjab v. Nestle India Ltd. support enforcing a government promise through a discretionary exemption power when promissory estoppel applies.

rule.if: is_appeal_from_denial_of_discretionary_tax_exemption and government_made_clear_exemption_promise and promisee_relied_and_changed_position and law_authorized_discretionary_exemption and officials_refused_to_exercise_discretion_without_considering_promise_and_reliance and requested_relief_does_not_require_general_rulemaking

predicates.is_appeal_from_denial_of_discretionary_t: The matter is an appeal arising from the denial of a claimed discretionary tax exemption.
predicates.government_made_clear_exemption_promise: The government made a clear representation that qualifying activity or property would receive a tax exemption.
predicates.promisee_relied_and_changed_position: The person to whom the representation was made relied on it and changed position by acting on that basis.
predicates.law_authorized_discretionary_exemption: A law authorized the government to decide whether to grant the relevant exemption.
predicates.officials_refused_to_exercise_discretion: Officials refused the exemption without taking account of the government’s promise and the claimant’s reliance on it.
predicates.requested_relief_does_not_require_genera: The relief sought can be granted by addressing the exercise of an existing discretionary power rather than requiring creation of general rules.

issues.definition: In an appeal from denial of a discretionary tax exemption, where a relied-upon government promise is within an existing statutory discretion and officials refuse to exercise that discretion without considering the promise and reliance, a court may remedy the arbitrary non-exercise if relief does not require general rulemaking.

issues.legal_issue: Promissory estoppel cannot support a tax exemption for a period when no statutory authority to grant that exemption remains in force.
material_facts: The provision authorizing the government to grant the tourism-related building-tax exemption was later omitted from the law.
The claim also sought exemption for a period after that statutory authority had ended.
issues.conclusion: No exemption relief could be granted for the period after the statutory authority to grant it had ended, because doing so would be contrary to law.
issues.legal_principle: M/S Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills holds that the government cannot be compelled by promissory estoppel to act contrary to statute. Promissory estoppel is an equitable doctrine and yields where enforcing the promise would require conduct unsupported by, or contrary to, the law then in force.

predicates.is_appeal_from_tax_exemption_denial: The matter is an appeal arising from the denial of a claimed tax exemption.
predicates.relief_is_sought_for_period_after_statut: The claimant seeks an exemption for a period after the law authorizing that exemption ceased to be in force.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a denied tax exemption and relief is sought for a period after statutory authority to grant it ended, exemption relief is unavailable for that period.
